claim: The llm-d scheduler pod generated by KServe LLMInferenceService runs the EPP and the KV-cache tracker as two separate containers in one pod, sharing state over ZeroMQ, with the EPP implementing pluggable routing scorers (queue-scorer, prefix-cache-scorer, max-score-picker).
stance_target: the EPP is a pluggable scheduler component distinct from the gateway proxy itself
scope_conditions: llm-d inference scheduler 0.7.1 on Amazon EKS, Red Hat AI Inference 3.4.0, Aug 2026
quoted_support: Container 1: main (scheduler): Image: registry.redhat.io/rhoai/odh-llm-d-inference-scheduler-rhel9. Runs the endpoint picker (EPP), which determines which backend pod to use. Implements routing plug-ins: queue-scorer, prefix-cache-scorer, and max-score-picker.

claim: The Envoy/Istio gateway pod has no direct Kubernetes API access at all; only the EPP scheduler and istiod watch the InferencePool custom resource, and istiod compiles it into the gateway's data-plane configuration so the gateway only ever calls the EPP over the pre-compiled ext-proc endpoint.
stance_target: architectural separation between the gateway data plane and the pod-selection control plane, relevant to whether a non-k8s-aware gateway could reuse the same EPP contract
scope_conditions: llm-d on Istio-based Gateway API implementation, EKS, Aug 2026
quoted_support: The scheduler Role has watch permissions and reads both resources directly from the Kubernetes API... The gateway pod does not have permission to access these resources... The gateway pod itself never reads from the Kubernetes API.

claim: InferencePool.spec.endpointPickerRef supports a failureMode of FailOpen (fall back to standard load balancing if the EPP is unreachable) or FailClose (drop requests instead), trading availability against routing-decision correctness.
stance_target: failure-mode design a custom non-k8s EPP integration would need to replicate
quoted_support: When you set failureMode: FailOpen, the gateway falls back to standard load balancing if the endpoint picker becomes unreachable... The alternative option is FailClose, which drops requests if the endpoint picker is unavailable.

claim: InferencePool and InferenceObjective belong to two different Kubernetes API groups (inference.networking.k8s.io and inference.networking.x-k8s.io respectively), and InferenceObjective priority is selected per-request via the client-set header x-gateway-inference-objective, defaulting to priority zero when omitted.
stance_target: exact API-shape details needed to replicate or bypass the EPP contract for non-k8s backends
scope_conditions: Gateway API Inference Extension, Aug 2026 versions (Gateway API 1.4.0, GIE 1.3.1)
quoted_support: A client selects an objective by setting the x-gateway-inference-objective header to the objective's name... Requests that omit the header fall back to the default treatment.

claim: The EPP's RBAC Role is scoped to read-only (get/list/watch) access on core pods/endpoints and on inferencepools/inferenceobjectives -- it cannot create, update, or delete any cluster resource.
stance_target: least-privilege design of the EPP that a non-k8s replacement backend would need to match or relax deliberately
quoted_support:
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods", "endpoints"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
- apiGroups: ["inference.networking.k8s.io", "inference.networking.x-k8s.io"]
  resources: ["inferencepools", "inferenceobjectives"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
